source.title: Interplay Between Optimization and Generalization of Stochastic Gradient Descent with Covariance Noise
source.authors: Yeming Wen; Kevin Luk; M. Gazeau; Guodong Zhang; Harris Chan; Jimmy Ba

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, though the title in the supplied metadata differs from the title shown in the text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether covariance noise can improve large-batch validation performance within a fixed epoch budget, using a different intervention from the cited large-batch studies.
record.gate_note: Table 2 reports validation accuracy for small-batch, large-batch, and large-batch with diagonal Fisher noise, trained for the same number of epochs within each row. The paper also cites prior work on batch size; those cited results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares small- and large-batch held-out accuracy under equal epoch budgets and tests covariance-noise interventions that can reduce the large-batch penalty. It tests V5 and is not an original source for that version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: diagonal Fisher noise improves large-batch validation accuracy while preserving desirable convergence under equal epoch budgets, but does not fully close every small-batch gap. The authors also emphasize that covariance structure explains optimization behavior better than gradient variance alone.
record.recipe_differences: Adds diagonal empirical Fisher covariance noise to large-batch gradient updates; the large-batch baseline uses Ghost Batch Normalization. The authors tune learning-rate schedules for each method and report a fixed epoch budget.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model change the size of the large-batch accuracy gap and how closely diagonal Fisher noise closes it; learning-rate schedule is tuned by method, and injected noise is terminated after one quarter of the training trajectory for best performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 5(b) reports lower maximum Hessian eigenvalues for diagonal-noise training than for baseline large-batch training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Diagonal Fisher noise lowers a calibrated Hessian-curvature measure. This does not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or its ranking of generalization gaps.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS) 2020; PMLR Volume 108.
record.problems: The reported metric is validation accuracy, not test error. Results are averaged over 3 random seeds, but the supplied text gives no numeric uncertainty intervals for Table 2. The comparison covers image classifiers only; large-batch with full Fisher was infeasible for most models.
record.rows_left_out: None of the Table 2 batch-regime validation-accuracy results were omitted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and interpolation thresholds.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under different tuning budgets.
Language models, workload-dependent batch thresholds, longer training, and isolated effects of warmup or normalization changes. These recipe choices are not independently ablated.
Dropout effects, small-data regimes, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, ranking train-test gaps, and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removal of examples selected by label memorization and subsequent accuracy changes.

missing.what: Seven numeric LB+Fisher Trace results are omitted: MLP/MNIST 98.08; LeNet/MNIST 99.02; LeNet/Fashion 90.29; VGG16/CIFAR-10 92.91; VGG16/CIFAR-100 71.35; ResNet44/CIFAR-10 92.33; ResNet44x2/CIFAR-100 73.77. These show how an alternative noise recipe changes the batch penalty under equal epochs.

Full Fisher noise reaches 93.22 on ResNet44/CIFAR-10 versus SB 93.42 and LB 91.93. The caption calls it roughly comparable to SB; report its substantial convergence cost and avoid assuming the same training budget without clarification.

Table 3 omits BatchChange accuracies 93.18, 72.44, 93.02 and 75.16; multiplicative-noise accuracies 90.98, 68.77, 91.28 and 71.98; and K-FAC-noise accuracies 93.06, 71.86, 92.81 and 73.84, respectively for VGG16/CIFAR-10, VGG16/CIFAR-100, ResNet44/CIFAR-10 and ResNet44x2/CIFAR-100. BatchChange uses SB for 50 epochs before LB; these comparisons document recipe dependence, although the appendix does not explicitly restate equal total epochs.

record.verdict_notes: States describe the large-batch accuracy penalty relative to SB; comparator rows cannot establish that penalty alone. All recorded values match Table 2. LB uses Ghost Batch Normalization; schedules are tuned separately, with scaling and warmup documented for the CIFAR experiments. Injected noise is stopped after one quarter of training. Validation accuracy is an appropriate held-out outcome for V5, but Table 2 supplies no numeric uncertainty beyond averaging three seeds. Partial recovery supports V5's existing qualification and does not by itself warrant limits_scope. The sentence claiming improvement over SB is inconsistent with most table entries; the demonstrated improvement is over LB. Missing-result verdicts await rows and clearer budget information where noted.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Language models; workload-dependent batch thresholds; the specific effects of longer training and normalization or regularization changes; some other adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of the train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

relationships.reason: R2, R5, R8, R11, R14, R17, R20, R23 and R26 are below their SB comparators by 0.15–3.38 percentage points despite tuned schedules and Ghost Batch Normalization.

relationships.condition: Diagonal Fisher noise on MNIST, MLP and LeNet, equal epochs
relationships.reason: R3 matches R1 at 98.10 and R6 reaches 99.11 versus R4's 99.10, supporting V5's allowance that adapted recipes can remove the penalty.
relationships.display_finding: With diagonal Fisher noise, which scales added noise using the diagonal of the Fisher information matrix, accuracy was 98.10% for the MLP and 99.11% for LeNet, versus small-batch accuracies of 98.10% and 99.10%. No uncertainty estimates were provided.

tranche.reason: Tests the same fixed-epoch batch-size/generalization question using a different intervention: structured covariance noise added to large-batch updates.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v4, dated February 2020, titled An Empirical Study of Large-Batch Stochastic Gradient Descent with Structured Covariance Noise; the pack uses an earlier title/year. Table 2 reports three-seed means without numerical uncertainty; Appendix A.7 specifies terminating injected noise after the first quarter of training, and V5 states require the SB comparisons alongside the intervention's LB baseline.
